vulnerable_statements.reason: The loop bound num_nodes comes from the PSP firmware's topology response and is never checked against the fixed size of the nodes[] array (AMDGPU_XGMI_MAX_CONNECTED_NODES). If num_nodes is larger than that, j can index past the end of the array.
When j is past the end of nodes[], this reads memory outside the array.
When j is past the end of nodes[], this writes outside the array and can corrupt nearby kernel memory in the psp/xgmi context.
Same out-of-bounds write as num_hops, at the same unchecked index j.

suggested_fix: Limit the loop index to the array size, e.g. `for (j = 0; j < min_t(int, mirror_top_info->num_nodes, AMDGPU_XGMI_MAX_CONNECTED_NODES); j++)`, or use ARRAY_SIZE(mirror_top_info->nodes). Better still, check num_nodes when the topology info is first received from the PSP, and reject or clamp any value larger than the nodes[] array so no consumer can index past it.
